figures.title: Chapter map
figures.why: one toolbox - add, resolve, project, cross - the map shows which tool answers which question
figures.read: an angle wants the dot, an area the cross, coplanarity the triple

figures.title: Adding vectors is not adding numbers
figures.why: the one intuition the chapter keeps returning to
figures.read: direction matters as much as length; the cosine term is the whole difference

figures.title: The dot product answers how much along
figures.why: work, components, and angle-finding are one machinery
figures.read: a scalar for projecting and angle-finding; perpendicular dots to zero

figures.title: The cross product answers how much around
figures.why: torque, angular momentum, magnetic force ask the same question
figures.read: a vector normal to both, magnitude the parallelogram area, sign flips on swap

figures.title: Scalar triple = signed volume, vector triple = BAC-CAB
figures.why: the two triple products are the standard confusables
figures.data: [a b c] = a·(b×c); a×(b×c) = b(a·c) - c(a·b)
figures.read: scalar triple tests coplanarity; vector triple is always BAC-CAB

figures.title: Triage - route by the keyword
figures.why: the keyword names the route before any number is touched
figures.read: angle wants the dot, area the cross, coplanarity the triple

drawings.title: The difference between a vector and a scalar
drawings.show: left: a temperature reading "37°C" (a number with a unit, no arrow). Right: a displacement "3 m east" (an arrow from a point, with the length representing 3 m and the direction pointing east). Below: two vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ drawn from the same point, with their sum $\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$ shown by the parallelogram diagonal.

drawings.title: The triangle and parallelogram laws
drawings.show: top: triangle law — vector $\mathbf{a}$ followed by vector $\mathbf{b}$, sum $\mathbf{c}$ closing the triangle. Bottom: parallelogram law — $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ from the same point, the diagonal showing $\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$, the other diagonal showing $\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b}$.

drawings.title: Components of a vector in 2D
drawings.show: a vector $\mathbf{a}$ of magnitude $a$ at angle $\theta$ from the $x$-axis; the $x$-component $a\cos\theta$ and $y$-component $a\sin\theta$ drawn as perpendicular projections onto the axes; the three sides of the right triangle labelled.
drawings.search: "vector components 2D x y cos sin theta diagram"

drawings.title: The dot product as projection
drawings.show: vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ with angle $\theta$ between them; the projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}$ shown as a dashed line from the head of $\mathbf{a}$ perpendicular to $\mathbf{b}$; the length of the projection labelled $a\cos\theta$; the formula $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}=ab\cos\theta$ shown alongside.
drawings.search: "dot product projection formula diagram angle between vectors"

drawings.title: The cross product and the right-hand rule
drawings.show: vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ lying in the $xy$-plane; $\mathbf{a}\times\mathbf{b}$ pointing in the $+z$ direction (right-hand rule); the magnitude $ab\sin\theta$ equal to the area of the parallelogram; the parallelogram shaded.
drawings.search: "cross product right hand rule area parallelogram diagram"

drawings.title: The scalar triple product as volume
drawings.show: three vectors $\mathbf{a}$, $\mathbf{b}$, $\mathbf{c}$ from a common origin forming a skewed box (parallelepiped); the base (parallelogram of $\mathbf{b}$ and $\mathbf{c}$) shaded; the height (component of $\mathbf{a}$ perpendicular to the base) shown as a dashed line; volume $=|\mathbf{b}\times\mathbf{c}|\times|a_{\perp}|$ annotated.

drawings.title: Solving $\mathbf{a}\times\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$
drawings.show: the vector $\mathbf{a}$ drawn vertically; $\mathbf{b}$ drawn perpendicular to $\mathbf{a}$ (the necessary condition $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}=0$); $\mathbf{x}$ drawn such that $\mathbf{a}\times\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$; the family of solutions $\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{x}_0+\lambda\mathbf{a}$ shown as a dashed line parallel to $\mathbf{a}$.
drawings.search: "vector equation cross product solution family diagram"

drawings.title: The polar basis and its rotation
drawings.show: the unit vectors $\hat{r}$ (pointing radially outward) and $\hat{\theta}$ (pointing tangentially, in the direction of increasing $\theta$) at a point on a circle; the angle $\theta$ from the $x$-axis; the rotation of $\hat{r}$ by $d\theta$ showing $d\hat{r}=\hat{\theta}\,d\theta$; the relation $\dot{\hat{r}}=\omega\hat{\theta}$ annotated.
drawings.search: "polar unit vectors r hat theta hat rotation time derivative diagram"

drawings.title: The scalar triple product as a signed volume
drawings.show: three vectors $\mathbf{a}$, $\mathbf{b}$, $\mathbf{c}$ forming a parallelepiped; the sign of $[\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathbf{c}]$ indicated by the right-hand rule: positive if $(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathbf{c})$ form a right-handed triad, negative if left-handed.
drawings.search: "scalar triple product signed volume right hand rule parallelepiped"

drawings.title: Vector addition in components
drawings.show: two vectors $\mathbf{a}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}$ and $\mathbf{b}=1\hat{i}+4\hat{j}$ drawn from the origin; their components shown as dashed projections onto the $x$ and $y$ axes; the sum $\mathbf{c}=4\hat{i}+6\hat{j}$ drawn as the diagonal of the parallelogram; each component of $\mathbf{c}$ shown as the sum of the corresponding components.
drawings.search: "vector addition components x y axis sum diagram"

drawings.title: The projection of a vector onto another
drawings.show: vector $\mathbf{a}$ at angle $\theta$ to vector $\mathbf{b}$; the projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}$ shown as a dashed line from the head of $\mathbf{a}$ perpendicular to $\mathbf{b}$; the length $a\cos\theta$ labelled; the projection vector $a\cos\theta\,\hat{b}$ drawn along $\mathbf{b}$.
drawings.search: "vector projection onto another vector dot product cos theta"

drawings.title: Anti-commutativity of the cross product
drawings.show: vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ in the $xy$-plane; $\mathbf{a}\times\mathbf{b}$ pointing in the $+z$ direction (out of page); $\mathbf{b}\times\mathbf{a}$ pointing in the $-z$ direction (into page); the magnitudes equal, the directions opposite; the right-hand rule applied to each.
drawings.search: "cross product anti commutativity a times b versus b times a"
